title: Saving with the part number unchanged leaves the number and open work alone
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test.
  • Create an open purchase order for this test, purchase order 1, from any vendor, with a line for part A picked from the lookup, 2 ordered and none received.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Replace the Sell Price with 22.00.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click the clock icon (Part History) at the left of the part A row.
  6. Click Parts in the top bar.
  7. Click Part Library in the left menu.
  8. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  9. Click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
  10. Open purchase order 1.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • Sell Price shows 22.00.

Step 4:

  • The change is saved and the window closes.

Step 5:

  • Part History's newest entry is the Sell Price change, and it has no "Part number updated" entry.

Step 6:

  • The Parts left menu shows Part Library.

Step 7:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 8:

  • Exactly one entry is listed, with part A's number.

Step 9:

  • The Purchase Orders list opens.

Step 10:

  • Purchase order 1's line still reads part A's number.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog), story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description)

  • S13-N3: “Saving with the number unchanged changes nothing about the number, the Part Library entry or open work.”
  • S7-N5b: “S7-N3 and S7-N4 apply when a part is created and when its part number is changed. Saving a part with its number unchanged is never refused by them, even when the location already holds a part whose number matches it.”
